convergenceSignals.reason: max-iterations policy requires review through iteration 10

findingDetails.title: Forced-depth validation can accept duplicate state records when the full range is present
findingDetails.evidence: forcedDepthIterationViolation applies unique() before comparing state iteration numbers with 1..cap, so a complete range plus a duplicate record is accepted when on-disk file count is complete.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reject duplicate state iteration numbers before set comparison and add complete-range-plus-duplicate fixtures for synthesis and artifact fallback paths.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Compared validator comments, state-record branch, on-disk count branch and focused duplicate/gap tests; no target writes.

adjudication.claim: The forced-depth validator does not enforce exactly one state record per iteration when all expected numbers are present.
adjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked the gapped-file and repeated-number fixtures, the synthesis path and the artifact-based fallback path.
adjudication.alternativeExplanation: Multiple state records may be intentional retries; rejected because the validator comment says each iteration ran once and no retry identity is modeled in this check.
adjudication.downgradeTrigger: Specify retry records as valid and add a separate attempt identity/counted event contract rather than calling the range exact-once.
